definitions.explanation: A person who has lost or failed, used as a derogatory label. Literally 'defeated dog.'
A person in a disadvantaged or inferior position, especially one who is mocked or dismissed by others.

examples.japanese: {負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}の{遠吠|とおぼ}え。
examples.english: Sour grapes. (Literally: the howling of a defeated dog.)

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}と{呼|よ}ばれるのが{嫌|いや}で、{必死|ひっし}に{努力|どりょく}した。
examples.english: He worked desperately because he hated being called a loser.

examples.japanese: {周|まわ}りから{負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}{扱|あつか}いされても、{自分|じぶん}の{信|しん}じる{道|みち}を{歩|ある}き{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: Even though treated as a loser by those around him, he kept walking the path he believed in.

examples.japanese: {負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}が{最後|さいご}に{逆転|ぎゃくてん}する{物語|ものがたり}は{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Stories where the underdog makes a comeback at the end are popular.

examples.japanese: いつも{負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}と{思|おも}われていたチームが{優勝|ゆうしょう}して、{大|おお}きな{話題|わだい}になった。
examples.english: The team that was always seen as the underdog won the championship and became big news.

examples.japanese: {負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}だった{選手|せんしゅ}が{何年|なんねん}もかけて{実力|じつりょく}をつけ、ついに{世界|せかい}{大会|たいかい}で{金|きん}メダルを{獲得|かくとく}した。
examples.english: The athlete who had been an underdog spent years building up their skills and finally won a gold medal at the world championship.

notes:
{負|ま}け{犬|いぬ} literally means "defeated dog." It is a derogatory term used to label someone as a loser or failure.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}の{遠吠|とおぼ}え (sour grapes; literally "howling of a defeated dog")
- {負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}{根性|こんじょう} (loser mentality)

The proverb {負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}の{遠吠|とおぼ}え describes someone who complains or boasts from a safe distance after losing, similar to the English expression "sour grapes." This is one of the most well-known uses of the word.

In the 2000s, the term gained a secondary usage to describe unmarried women over 30 without children, popularized by a bestselling book. This usage was controversial and is now considered outdated.
